newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian Defense Minister denies drug payoff.
newsitem.headline: Colombian Defense Minister denies drug payoff.

text.p: Defence Minister Guillermo Alberto Gonzalez said on Friday that a check apparently signed by a drug kingpin entered his campaign coffers when he ran for Congress in the 1980s.
But he denied having personally accepted any money from billionaire cocaine trafficker Justo Pastor Perafan and said the check was drawn on someone else's account.

The case opens the door to another possible drug corruption scandal in Colombia. Gonzalez grew up in the same town as Perafan and was linked to him in press reports before he took office just last month.
In a public statement, Gonzalez said he had asked the prosecutor-general's office to investigate the origin of the check and probe his personal wealth if necessary.
The statement said the $3,000 check was drawn on an account with Colombia's Banco Ganadero belonging to a man it identified as Luis Fernando Escobar Callejas.

Gonzalez said he had no idea who Escobar Callejas was, but he conceded that the check appeared to be signed by Perafan, a drug lord who has been the target of a nationwide manhunt since authorities ordered his arrest on the drug-related charge of illicit enrichment in February of last year.

Adding an element of confusion to his explanation about the check, which Gonzalez said was brought to his attention on Monday, he said it was unclear whether his aides had accepted it in 1984 or 1989. He ran for Congress in both those years.
A spokesman for the prosecutor-general's confirmed that the check was the target of an investigation that had been opened at Gonzalez's request but was unable to clarify when it was written.

Perafan, a former army sergeant whose personal wealth has been estimated at $12 billion, is said to have business interests in Madrid, Moscow and Rome as well as Colombia, where his holdings including a sprawling estate on Isla Baru island off the Caribbean port city of Cartagena.
According to Dinero, Colombia's leading financial news magazine, his crimes include the shipment of up to more than 4,400 pounds (2,000 kg) of cocaine to Italy and other countries.

Gonzalez and Perafan, both in their 50s, grew up in the town of Popayan in southwest Cauca province and Gonzalez has admitted having had social contacts with him in the past, while serving as ambassdor to Brazil and in Europe.
President Ernesto Samper, who has been dogged by allegations that he financed his own 1994 campaign with drug money, expressed support for Gonzalez in remarks to reporters on Friday afternoon.
"The government is at peace regarding the minister's innocence, that's why he is still in the cabinet," he said.

Samper's first defence minister, Fernando Botero, served as his campaign manager before taking office. He has been detained at a military base in Bogota since August 1995 on charges stemming from the alleged illicit financing of Samper's campaign.
